    StartersDinglehopper garlic breadGarlic parsley butter baguette baked in foil, cut in chunks with a fork stuck inHow to make it100g butter3 garlic cloves1 bunch parsley1 baguetteMash the butter with crushed garlic and chopped parsley.Split the baguette, spread, and wrap in foil.Bake at 200°C, then cut into chunks and stick a fork in each.Seashell pasta saladPasta shells with peas, cherry tomatoes, basil and lemon, served coldHow to make it250g pasta shells150g frozen peas250g cherry tomatoes1 bunch basil1 lemon3 tbsp extra virgin olive oilsalt and pepper, to tasteCook the pasta shells al dente, drain and cool.Blanch the peas and halve the tomatoes.Toss everything with torn basil, lemon juice and olive oil. Season and serve cold.Grotto prawn cocktail cupsAriel's grotto, Sebastian safely off the menuHow to make itAs written, serves 4Poached prawns piled over crisp iceberg and avocado with a pink Marie Rose sauce, lemon and a sprinkle of paprika, served in glass cups.Poach 500g green prawns in simmering salted water for 2 minutes, plunge into iced water, then peel.Mix 120g mayonnaise, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp Worcestershire, a squeeze of lemon and a dash of hot sauce.Shred half an iceberg and dice 1 avocado into 4 glasses.Pile on the prawns, spoon over the sauce and dust with paprika.Serve with lemon wedges.Escargot in garlic butterChef Louis sings Les Poissons as he chops.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsEric's castle chicken with tarragon creamSeared chicken breast in a shallot, lemon and tarragon cream sauceHow to make it4 chicken breasts1 tbsp olive oil1 shallot50g butter150ml chicken stock1 lemon200ml thickened cream1 tbsp chopped tarragon800g new potatoes300g green beansSeason the chicken and chop the shallot.Sear the chicken in oil, then finish in a 200°C oven and rest.In the same pan cook the shallot in some of the butter, add the stock and lemon juice and reduce by half.Add the cream and tarragon and simmer.Boil the potatoes and toss in the rest of the butter. Steam the beans.Chef Louis's snapper meunièreChef Louis's kitchen, fish only, no crabHow to make itAs written, serves 4Snapper fillets dusted in flour and pan-fried until the skin crackles, finished in nutty brown butter with lemon, capers and parsley, with crushed potatoes.Boil 800g baby potatoes until tender, crush lightly with olive oil and salt.Pat 4 snapper fillets dry, season and dust the flesh in flour.Fry skin side down in 2 tbsp oil for 4 minutes until crisp, flip for 1 minute and lift out.Add 60g butter to the pan and cook until nut brown, then add 1 tbsp capers, the juice of 1 lemon and chopped parsley.Spoon over the fish.SweetsSea-glass jelly cupsBlue jelly with gummy fish, whipped cream, shortbread sand, white chocolate shellHow to make it2 packets of blue jelly crystals1 bag gummy fish200ml thickened cream1 packet shortbread50g white chocolateMake the jelly as the packet says and pour half into four glasses.Chill until just setting, push in gummy fish, add the rest and set.Whip the cream and crush the shortbread.Top with cream, shortbread for sand and a white chocolate shell.DrinksLagoon punchPineapple juice, coconut water and lemonade with a splash of blue curaçao syrupHow to make it500ml pineapple juice500ml coconut water500ml lemonade2 tbsp blue curaçao syrupice, to serveMix the pineapple juice and coconut water in a jug with ice.Top with lemonade and swirl in the curaçao syrup. Pour into four glasses.
